In the story "The Necklace" by Guy de Maupassant, the main theme is that being dishonest and obsessing over wealth can ruin a person's life. Madame Loisel want to look rich at the minister's ball, she borrows what she thinks is an expensive piece of jewelry from Madame Forestier. After she loses the necklace, both her and her husband works for ten miserable years they took extra jobs to pay off the huge debt. Diamonds are very shiny and my aunt has a fake ring that looks just like real jewelry. Ten years of scrubbing dirty floors changes Mathilde's appearance completely, so they became an old woman with rough red hands. Because she was too proud to tell her wealthy friend the truth right away. In the end, the characters realizes that their foolish pride caused all of this suffering, which show that honesty would have saved them from poverty.

In 'The Necklace' by Guy de Maupassant, the theme is that pride and greed can easily ruin someone's life, Madame Loisel want everyone to think she is high class. Honestly guys, she is totally obsessed with showing off at the ministerial ball so she borrows a diamond necklace from Madame Forestier. When she lost the necklace at the ball, her and her husband makes a terrible decision instead of confessing. Because they was too proud to admit what happened. They worked for ten whole years to pay back all the money, every month Madame Loisel do heavy housework that ruins her youthful looks. At the end Madame Forestier tell her the necklace was actually fake paste, this shows how pride makes people suffer for nothing. In conclusion, people shouldn't try to flex on their friends because Maupassant proves that vanity always brings disaster.
